draft.title: Churches in Australian society
card: Before 1945, churches did much more than hold services. They ran schools, hospitals and charities, and many people met these services in daily life.
Schools
Churches set up many schools. Catholic schools, for example, taught children in the faith as well as in other subjects.
Hospitals and charities
Churches ran hospitals and charities that helped the sick, the poor and orphaned children. Many of these services were run by church members and religious orders.
Laws
Church leaders and members also pushed for laws on moral issues. Two examples are drinking and trading on Sundays, and they influenced these laws, though they did not always win.
draft.remember: Churches shaped daily life through services they ran and laws they pushed for.

a.q: A church in 1900 runs a hospital and a school in a country town. What does this best show about churches then?
opts: They played a role in community life beyond worship
They were the only providers of services in Australia
They controlled all laws passed by parliaments
They ran services only for their own church members
a.why: Running a hospital and a school shows churches serving the community in daily life, not just holding services. The card does not say churches were the only providers or controlled every law, so the other options claim too much.
a.clue: Think about what the church does besides worship.

b.q: In the 1890s, members of a church group in Ballarat campaign for shops and hotels to close on Sundays. Which description fits this best?
opts: Church members trying to influence laws on Sunday trading
Church members running a charity for people in need
Church members setting up a school for local children
Church members taking over the work of parliament
b.why: Campaigning for closing times is an attempt to influence law, which the card gives as Sunday trading. Running a charity is a different church activity, and the group is lobbying, not taking over parliament.
b.clue: The group wants to change a rule, not provide a service.

a.best: They played a role in community life beyond worship

b.best: Church members trying to influence laws on Sunday trading

problems.detail: 'Services' is used in two senses in one bullet: 'did much more than hold services' means worship, then 'many people met these services' means schools, hospitals and charities. This can confuse students. The remember line ('services they ran') and option a4 carry the same ambiguity.
The clue 'Think about what the church does besides worship' echoes the right option's 'beyond worship', so it gives the answer away.

All three distractors use absolute words ('the only providers', 'controlled all laws', 'only for their own church members'). The hedged right option stands out, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

The clue 'wants to change a rule, not provide a service' rules out the charity and school options outright. That leaves only the obviously extreme 'taking over the work of parliament', so the clue all but gives the answer. The stem's 'close on Sundays' also matches the right option's 'Sunday trading' word for word.

proposal.title: Churches in Australian society
card: Before 1945, churches did much more than lead worship. They ran schools, hospitals and charities that many Australians relied on in daily life.
Schools
Churches set up many schools. Catholic schools, for example, taught children the faith alongside other subjects.
Hospitals and charities
Churches ran hospitals and charities that cared for the sick, the poor and orphaned children. Church members and religious orders, groups who commit their lives to their faith, did much of this work.
Laws

Church leaders and members also pressed parliaments for laws on moral issues, such as limits on drinking alcohol and on trading on Sundays. Parliaments made the laws, and churches did not always get what they wanted.
proposal.remember: Churches shaped daily life through the care and teaching they gave and the laws they campaigned for.

a.q: A church in 1900 runs a hospital and a school in a country town. What does this best show about churches then?
opts: They took part in the wider life of the community
They mainly focused on holding weekly worship
They worked mostly to change the laws of the colony
They left health and education to the government
a.why: A hospital and a school serve the whole town in everyday life, so the church's role reached well past worship. Changing laws was another church activity, but running a hospital and school is not lawmaking.
a.clue: Who in the town would use a hospital and a school?

b.q: In 1915, members of a church group in Ballarat petition the Victorian parliament to make hotels stop serving alcohol at 6 pm. Which description fits this best?
opts: Church members trying to influence a law on drinking
Church members passing a law on hotel closing times
Church members running a charity for drinkers' families
Church members teaching about alcohol in a church school
b.why: A petition asks parliament to act, so the group is trying to influence a law on drinking. The group cannot pass the law itself, because parliaments make the laws. No charity or school is involved here.
b.clue: Look at who the petition is sent to.

a.best: They took part in the wider life of the community

b.best: Church members trying to influence a law on drinking
